# Maintenance Scheduling Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Maintenance Scheduling Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness. Building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved maintenance environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded maintenance files, proposed plant sources, Microsoft Teams and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypass them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger. Record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for condition monitoring, CMMS, MES, parts and roster data, and Teams collaboration. No customer connection is needed for the synthetic workshop. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare maintenance, production, operations and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview, not publication. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files, with no PAC CLI or YAML import. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Maintenance rule ownership | Have maintenance owners replace the fictional probabilities, durations, costs and readiness notes before customer data is used. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Maintenance business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Coordination effort across condition, history, capacity, parts, backup and production systems before a maintenance decision. Establish how separate systems slow maintenance planning before crediting any change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Asset | Measurement period | Condition signal | Systems consulted | Planning effort | Unplanned downtime events | Approver |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree maintenance replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Maintenance business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Maintenance business owner | Approve maintenance sources, planning scope and the approval workflow; agree production success measures without treating synthetic figures as results. |
| Authorized maintenance and production owners | Verify telemetry and approve any action through connected CMMS, MES and safety systems. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent in Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing and capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any plant connection is approved. |
| Plant system connection owners | Approve dedicated references for condition monitoring, work management, production schedules, parts, rosters and collaboration; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check MS-01 through MS-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; fail any claim of equipment control, work creation, assignment or dispatch. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route maintenance decisions to authorized owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Maintenance replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures have named agreement.
- [ ] The maintenance owner records where condition, history, capacity, parts, backup and production evidence live today before choosing measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/maintenance-scheduling/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The customer confirms authenticated audience and least-privilege access for plant, staff and cost data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/maintenance-scheduling/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/maintenance-scheduling/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/maintenance-scheduling/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/maintenance-scheduling/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Maintenance Scheduling Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_maintenance-scheduling-review-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_maintenance-scheduling-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_downtime_analysis
9. Add skill: aibast_predictive_alerts
10. Add skill: aibast_schedule_overview
11. Add skill: aibast_work_order_plan
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass MS-01: Maintenance Manager
15. Pass MS-02: Production Supervisor
16. Pass MS-03: Maintenance Manager
17. Pass MS-04: Operations Leader
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: MS-01, MS-02, MS-03, MS-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `MaintenanceSchedulingAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The optional Brainstem lane is recorded as used or skipped; no workshop step depends on it.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged maintenance prompt passes once in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full response; annotated screenshots do not replace the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before showing plant, staff or cost information. Request only read scopes for approved condition, work, production and resource data. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved condition monitoring and IoT

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant system connection owners

1. **Bind Approved condition monitoring and IoT — read:** Bind least-privilege read-only telemetry actions.

2. **Identity for Approved condition monitoring and IoT:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved condition monitoring and IoT:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved condition monitoring and IoT:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Imply no live access; the readings are a fixed synthetic snapshot. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim live telemetry, a work order or a dispatch.

### Step 3-2. Integrate CMMS work management

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant system connection owners

1. **Bind CMMS work management — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any work-order creation behind authorization (preview).

2. **Identity for CMMS work management:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope CMMS work management:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for CMMS work management:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Create and dispatch nothing; end the proposed plan with `No work order is created or dispatched.` [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim live telemetry, a work order or a dispatch.

### Step 3-3. Integrate MES production schedules

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant system connection owners

1. **Bind MES production schedules — read:** Bind approved read-only schedule actions.

2. **Identity for MES production schedules:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope MES production schedules:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for MES production schedules:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no production schedule; backup readiness is a planning note that needs production-fit review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a proposal and name the authorization gate; execute nothing.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Approved resource and collaboration systems

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant system connection owners

1. **Bind Approved resource and collaboration systems — read-write:** Start read-only; gate reservations, assignments and messages behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved resource and collaboration systems:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved resource and collaboration systems:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved resource and collaboration systems:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Reserve no part; parts readiness is a planning state. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return a proposal and name the authorization gate; execute nothing.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Plant system connection owners

Create read tools with dedicated references for approved condition, asset, work, parts, technician, backup and production data.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Condition, asset, work, parts, production, reporting and collaboration sources use dedicated, verified connection references.
- [ ] Action tools for equipment commands, work creation, assignment, dispatch, reservation or production change stay unavailable until explicitly authorized.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Before rollout, test an approved test deployment as maintenance, production and operations users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data measures; synthetic probabilities, scores, durations and costs are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked maintenance corpus | All four cases, MS-01 through MS-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Operational control boundary | Any claim of equipment control, work-order creation, assignment, scheduling, dispatch, reservation or production change is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a positive target-state anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required images. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Maintenance business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Maintenance business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved maintenance audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed maintenance sessions, their transcripts, tool connection and authentication errors, and credit use in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

### Customer or partner delivers
